When opponents drop, wherever it lands, Chen loses the point within two shots 2% of the time (n=92, 95% CI 1%-8%); typical pros lose 10% after the same shot (difference -8 points, 95% CI -10 to -2, n=7228).

When Chen smashes to the opponent's mid backhand, Chen loses the point within two shots 0% of the time (n=75, 95% CI 0%-5%); typical pros lose 6% after the same shot (difference -6 points, 95% CI -7 to -1, n=4094).

When opponents play a net shot to Chen's front forehand, Chen loses the point within two shots 21% of the time (n=121, 95% CI 14%-29%); typical pros lose 13% after the same shot (difference +7 points, 95% CI +1 to +16, n=7040).

When Chen pushes or rushes to the opponent's rear forehand, Chen loses the point within two shots 16% of the time (n=44, 95% CI 8%-29%); typical pros lose 7% after the same shot (difference +9 points, 95% CI +1 to +23, n=1902).

xp.caveat: Read this first: xP from shot and position data has no signal mid-rally in elite singles (holdout AUC 0.50 on strokes that did not end the rally). The same features reach AUC 0.79 only on final strokes, where the task is classifying how an already-decisive stroke ends (winner or error), not predicting a rally. Nothing in this section is a working expected-points model.
